items.title: 浅谈一下使用Claude和ChatGPT的感受
items.summary:
浅谈一下使用Claude和ChatGPT的感受

我是GPT和claude 双会员，而且都开到最高级了

GPT给我的感觉就是一个非常牛逼的博士生，它的后台框架能力很强，codex的代码编程水平很高，而且很省，我个人觉得后台它比claude做的好，有什么bug你跟它讲它立刻就能修复的让你满意。

但是GPT的问题是以下几个：

第一，它的前端审美一坨屎，几乎没有审美，你说它是理科生审美都是在骂理科生。

第二，不爱说人话，你不论跟它说什么，它都要跟你平衡，仿佛你说太阳是东升西江，它也要特意跟你说在当前情况下的的地球是这样的，就是不喜欢强调绝对性语句，一定要保持它那该死的客观公正的态势。

比如我问他我身体不舒服大概什么原因，他说了半天我字都认识，就是不知道它想说什么。

然后就是GPT属于你的框架知识越足够，准备的越充分，它越厉害，你不说的地方它半点不做，它不会多干一点，简直就像博士生毕业之前的状态。

Claude 的一个巨大的优点就是理解审美，理解语言，而且claude在我个人感觉它的某一些地方相当恐怖。

它能get到我的喜好，而且像一个超级牛逼会读心术的舔狗，你不需要像调教GPT一样，你说一句他干一句。claude会直接提前帮你规划好几步，甚至把你个人常用的一些手法和方式都融入进来，哪怕你没说，我严重怀疑claude在分析用户做用户情绪监测。

其次，claude有一些很吓人的体验经历，比如我有一次在做游戏项目开发，用claude跑代码，然后claude突然给我来了一句我的电脑有木马，让我删除，申请它来执行，然后它不仅找到了这一个，一会给我把电脑所有的木马记录和执行记录以及信息输送的经过全部告诉我了。

但你要知道，这不是我主动要求它做的，而是它自然而然的突然在开发游戏的过程中发现了一个毫不相关的进程。

这件事当时就让我蒙圈了，我真的完全想不到agent到了这种可怕的地步，它是建立了一个监测程序专门去盯着cpu进程，因为它觉得自己运行效率太低了，结果发现了木马，然后它没有问，直接就开始追踪，结果找到7个，还自动化运行清理，最后发现需要管理员，才让我搞。

如果你不理解吓人的地方在哪，那就当我没说。

我用GPT已经很久很久了，从来没有出现过这种情况它就像个傻子一样每天在那说废话，有时候规划任务都规划半天，之前我是不敢给claude权限，但是GPT的前端开发噪声太大了，我嫌弃它听不懂我说什么换claude，一个月进度翻了5倍。

我现在就是让claude 管着gpt做后台，效率很高。

以上仅代表个人使用感受，有其他想法或者意见欢迎一起交流。

items.title: LLMの翻訳に対する人間の修正履歴をRAGとして再利用するHuman-in-the-loopは有効か？
items.summary:
LLMの翻訳に対する人間の修正履歴をRAGとして再利用するHuman-in-the-loopは有効か？

→結論：有効。 過去の修正履歴を検索し、In-context Learning（ICL）で再利用することで、Fine-tuningなしに翻訳精度を改善できた。ただし、単純に修正例を追加するだけでは性能が悪化する場合もある。

MT Summit 2023（被引用数：約50件）

背景

マカオ大学の研究チームによる研究。従来の機械翻訳では、人間の修正をモデルに反映するためにFine-tuningが必要だった。そこで、修正履歴を外部DBに蓄積し、LLMの推論時に再利用するHuman-in-the-loopを提案。

方法

GPT-3.5-Turboを使用し、ドイツ語→英語翻訳を5領域（IT、宗教、法律、医療、字幕）で評価。
正解訳との差分から修正指示を自動生成し、人間のフィードバックを模擬。
過去の類似した修正履歴をBM25で検索し、Few-shot ICLで翻訳を修正。
修正前後の翻訳をLLM自身に比較させる方法も検証。

結果

修正履歴を単純に与えるだけでは、翻訳精度が低下する場合があった。
修正前後を比較して選択する方法では、5領域すべてでBLEUが改善（最大+0.9ポイント）。
実際の人間による修正や作業効率の改善は未検証。

タイトル： Human-in-the-loop Machine Translation with Large Language Model

# Calc Unit 6: Indefinite Integration

By K Dodd

🖶 Printer-friendly version

An indefinite integral is exactly the same thing as an anti-derivative - they are synonyms.

Many functions can have the same derivative since the derivative of a constant is zero. For example, the following functions all have the same derivative of 3x2:

 x3
 x3 + 1
 x3 - 4
 x3 + π [...] The symbol used for integration is an integral sign ∫ where the following expression means that you are looking for the anti-derivative of f(x). [...] ⑦ Sometimes, the easiest approach to taking an anti-derivative is to first algebraically simplify its derivative. For example

∫(2x−3)2dx

If this derivative had been created by using the chain rule, you should see a product. But there is no product, just a squared binomial. So our first trick is to algebraically multiply out the derivative. Then we will have a sum of x-terms that we can integrate with the reverse power rule.

At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said. [...] "When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand," Friar told CNBC's Sara Eisen in an interview at the Citi TMT Leadership Summit at California's Pebble Beach. "It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital."

items.title: Exclusive: OpenAI targets Microsoft's GitHub with deal
items.summary:
OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer, a developer tools startup whose technology is already embedded in Codex, the company told Axios exclusively.

Why it matters:OpenAI is joining a slew of companies challenging Microsoft's GitHub as AI agents take on more coding work. The platform has acted as a central repository and nerve center for software development for many years.

Zoom out:GitHub has faced a number of reliability issues and outages as AI coding has taken off. [...] Financial terms were not disclosed. Pierre's open-source projects will remain open-source.

Between the lines:Earlier this week, OpenAI revealed Pando, built to handle the explosion of code generated by AI agents.

   OpenAI says Pando reduced the time needed to push code changes by nearly 80%. 
   The company is now exploring ways to make the technology available to customers. [...] Cursor, now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, launched GitHub rival Origin in August.
   Former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, who launched a new coding startup, announced a competing product last month.
   Microsoft owns nearly a quarter of OpenAI, although the two companies also compete in a variety of ways, a dynamic that is common across the competitive AI landscape.

Driving the news: OpenAI plans to integrate Pierre's Code Storage function into Codex, where Pierre's technology is already used.
